element.name: Market Agility & Competitive Pressure
element.documentation: In an AI-driven landscape the "cost of delay" is existential. If the bank cannot deliver features as fast as a startup or a tech giant, it loses market share.

element.name: Regulatory Resiliency & Social License
element.documentation: For a major financial institution, non-compliance with APRA CPS 230/234 is a threat to the banking license. Manual compliance is too slow and error-prone for an AI-speed world.

element.name: Systemic Sustainability & Complexity Management
element.documentation: Unmanaged architectural drift creates hidden debt that makes systems fragile. Left unchecked, the system eventually becomes too complex to change at any speed.

element.name: Human-to-Machine Operational Scaling
element.documentation: Human architects are a finite bottleneck. As AI agents produce changes at machine speed, it is physically impossible to review it all with traditional methods.

element.name: Executive Leadership & Board
element.documentation: Accountable for the banking licence, market position and the enterprise risk appetite. Holds the agility and compliance drivers.

element.name: Prudential Regulator (APRA)
element.documentation: External stakeholder. Requires demonstrable, continuous compliance with CPS 230/234 and sound model risk management.

element.name: Enterprise Architecture Function
element.documentation: Owns architectural coherence and the target state; carries the sustainability and complexity-management concern.

element.name: Delivery Organisation
element.documentation: Human engineers and AI delivery agents producing change at machine speed; holds the operational-scaling concern.

element.name: Risk & Compliance Function
element.documentation: Second-line assurance. Needs provable, auditable control effectiveness rather than after-the-fact manual evidence.

element.name: Human review cannot keep pace with AI-speed delivery
element.documentation: Change volume from AI agents already exceeds what human architects and reviewers can inspect; the gap widens monthly.

element.name: Architectural drift is accumulating as unmanaged risk
element.documentation: As-built systems diverge from intent with no systematic detection; hidden architectural debt is compounding.

element.name: Manual compliance evidence is too slow and error-prone
element.documentation: Control mapping and evidence collection are manual, lag delivery by weeks, and cannot be trusted at AI-delivery cadence.

element.name: Frictionless Architecture & Governance at Machine Speed
element.documentation: Sustain architecturally-sound, provably-compliant change at the speed and volume of AI-driven delivery — without a human review bottleneck and without accumulating unmanaged architectural drift.

element.name: Architecture as Executable Intelligence
element.documentation: Architecture has moved from passive documentation to executable system intelligence: the specification, the controls, and the guardrails are machine-readable artefacts that AI agents and pipelines consume directly.

element.name: Deterministic Human Accountability
element.documentation: AI is advisory; the specification is deterministic; a human holds sign-off.

element.name: Forensic Auditability
element.documentation: Ability to reconstruct not just what happened but why a decision was made.

element.name: Policy as Code
element.documentation: All governance rules, compliance mappings, and architectural guardrails are expressed as version-controlled, machine-executable policy, not prose documents.

element.name: APRA CPS 230/234 Compliance
element.documentation: Operational resilience and prudential standards.

element.name: Model Risk Management (SR 11-7 / APRA)
element.documentation: Validation, documentation, and oversight obligations for models and agentic decision-making. SR 11-7 is the de facto global standard adopted by major banks; APRA's prudential and operational-resilience guidance sets the Australian expectation. Together they govern how autonomous decisions are validated, evidenced, and supervised.

element.name: Australian Privacy Act (APP)
element.documentation: Data privacy and protection regulations.

element.name: Cloud & Data Sovereignty Policy
element.documentation: Governance and compliance policies for cloud-based operations.

element.name: Automated Specification Generation from Graph
element.documentation: For every approved change request, the system must automatically derive a complete, executable architectural specification from the knowledge graph — with zero manual authoring by an architect.

element.name: Automated Regulatory Obligation Mapping
element.documentation: Every technical change must be automatically mapped to its applicable APRA CPS 230/234 obligations before a deployment gate is passed. No change may proceed without a resolved compliance mapping.

element.name: Pre-Deployment Compliance Gate Enforcement
element.documentation: The supervisory control plane must intercept and evaluate all agent-generated changes against the executable specification before they reach any test or production environment. Non-compliant changes must be blocked, not flagged retrospectively.

element.name: Continuous As-Built vs. As-Designed Reconciliation
element.documentation: The system must continuously reconcile observed system state (telemetry, deployed artefacts) against the knowledge graph's as-designed intent and surface any deviation as a classified drift event.

element.name: Mandatory Human Sign-off for Non-Standard Changes
element.documentation: Any change that cannot be deterministically validated against the executable specification must be escalated to a named human architect for explicit approval. The system must prevent autonomous resolution of ambiguous compliance cases.

element.name: Maintained Machine-Readable Control Catalog
element.documentation: The platform must maintain the full set of applicable regulatory obligations, policies and standards as version-controlled, machine-readable control definitions (OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles), kept synchronised with upstream regulatory content sources.

element.name: Curated Reusable Architecture Library
element.documentation: The platform must maintain a curated library of technology-agnostic architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and composed solution designs — each mapped to its applicable controls and threat model — as the reuse basis for all new solution architecture and specification generation.

element.name: Authoritative Digital Twin of System State
element.documentation: The platform must maintain a live, queryable graph of enterprise technology state — an intent plane and an as-built digital twin plane — as the single authoritative source of architectural truth that every other capability reads from.

element.name: Immutable Forensic Audit Ledger
element.documentation: Every agent action, gate decision, specification evaluation and governed state transition must be recorded to an append-only, queryable ledger usable as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Management
element.documentation: Maintain a live, queryable graph of the enterprise technology landscape — its components, policies, relationships, and regulatory mappings, across an intent plane and an as-built twin plane — as the authoritative source of architectural truth.

element.name: Executable Specification Generation
element.documentation: Deterministically produce machine-consumable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph, which AI agents and CI/CD pipelines consume as guardrails rather than human-readable documents.

element.name: Agentic Development Supervision
element.documentation: Constrain, monitor, and intervene in the behaviour of autonomous development agents in real time, enforcing architectural and regulatory boundaries before code reaches any environment.

element.name: Forensic Audit Recording
element.documentation: Record every agent action, gate decision, and specification evaluation into an immutable, queryable ledger that serves as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Architectural Drift Detection & Reconciliation
element.documentation: Continuously compare observed system telemetry against the as-designed knowledge graph and surface deviations — strategic, structural, or agentic — in real time.

element.name: Human Oversight & Approval
element.documentation: Identify, route, and manage human architect approval for changes that deviate from deterministic specifications or present ambiguous compliance scenarios, through a defined, auditable sign-off process that upholds deterministic human accountability.

element.name: Control & Obligation Management
element.documentation: Maintain the authoritative, version-controlled library of control and compliance content — external regulatory obligations and the organisation's own policies, standards and controls alike — as OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles kept synchronised with upstream regulatory sources, and map every governed change to its applicable obligations.

element.name: Reusable Architecture Curation
element.documentation: Curate technology-agnostic architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and composed solution designs — with control mappings and threat models — as the reusable basis for new solution architecture and specification generation, and model candidate and future-state architecture options for governance decisions.

element.name: Shift Governance Into the Pipeline
element.documentation: Replace document-and-meeting governance with machine-readable specifications, controls and enforcement gates that run inline with delivery.

element.name: Operate a Living Architecture Twin
element.documentation: Maintain an authoritative, continuously-reconciled model of intended and actual architecture as the single source both humans and agents work from.

element.name: Curate Reuse Before Build
element.documentation: Make curated patterns, blueprints and control mappings the default starting point for every change, rather than bespoke design.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Intangible resource — the graph of intent, controls, patterns and as-built state.

element.name: AI Delivery Agents
element.documentation: Human-equivalent resource — the agentic crew that produces change at machine speed.

element.name: OSCAL Control Content
element.documentation: Intangible resource — the machine-readable regulatory and control corpus.

element.name: Enterprise Architecture Practice
element.documentation: Human resource — the architects who curate patterns and hold governance decisions.

element.name: Governed Architecture Delivery
element.documentation: End-to-end value stream that turns an approved change into a compliant, twin-reconciled production release: baseline, specify, build, prove, release, reconcile.

element.name: Establish Control & Reuse Baseline
element.documentation: Curated controls, obligations, patterns and blueprints are in place to build the change against.

element.name: Specify the Change
element.documentation: A deterministic, executable specification is derived from the knowledge graph for the approved change.

element.name: Build Under Supervision
element.documentation: Development agents produce code, tests and manifests within enforced architectural and regulatory boundaries.

element.name: Prove Compliance
element.documentation: The release candidate is evaluated against the specification and the expected controls; non-compliant changes are blocked, not flagged later.

element.name: Release & Attest
element.documentation: A compliant release is deployed, human sign-off is captured where required, and every decision is recorded to the forensic ledger.

element.name: Reconcile & Remediate
element.documentation: Observed state is continuously reconciled against intent and classified drift is routed to remediation.

element.name: Deterministic Spec Generation
element.documentation: Scripted, template-driven generation of executable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph. AI recommends scope; human holds sign-off. Output is the deterministic intent consumed by the agentic crew.

element.name: Agentic Development Execution
element.documentation: Supervised execution of AI-driven development within supervisory control plane constraints. Consumes the executable specification, regulation, policy, patterns, and controls from the knowledge graph to generate code, test suites, and deployment manifests.

element.name: Automated CICD Gate Execution
element.documentation: The CI/CD pipeline with the agentic control plane woven in. Evaluates every artefact against the executable specification and policy-as-code gates before a release is permitted. Blocks on violation; escalates exceptions for human review; logs all gate outcomes to the immutable ledger.

element.name: Production Release
element.documentation: Compliant, traceable-to-spec deployment to production, triggered only after all gates have cleared. Automatically auditable end-to-end.

element.name: Current State Discovery
element.documentation: Continuous, automated reconciliation of actual system state against architectural intent. Surfaces classified drift events for human review; does not write directly to the backlog.

element.name: Drift Review & Triage Gate
element.documentation: Human-gated review of drift findings before they are committed as backlog work items. A Solution Architect approves architectural drift; Security & Compliance approves regulatory drift. Ensures only validated, prioritised findings enter the delivery pipeline.

element.name: Frictionless Architecture Platform
element.documentation: Governs architecture from authored policy through to BAU control effectiveness.

element.name: Controls & Compliance Catalog
element.documentation: Authors custom policies and standards and converts them to OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles.

element.name: Reusable Architecture Library
element.documentation: Composable patterns, blueprints and solution designs with OSCAL references, threat modelling, and modelling of candidate / future-state options for governance to decide on.

element.name: Digital Twin & Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Maintains the Architecture Knowledge Graph: an intent plane and a current-state digital twin plane.

element.name: Architecture Governance
element.documentation: Comparative evaluation of candidate options, impact assessment, the decision and its ADR, and archival of the rejected options with reasons. Pure decision-making — the options themselves are modelled in the Reusable Architecture Library.

element.name: Conformance & Drift Assurance
element.documentation: Enforces controls at release, monitors effectiveness in BAU, and detects and reports architecture drift.

element.name: Modelling & Specification
element.documentation: Out-of-the-box ArchiMate / C4 / UML modelling, and generation of development specifications.

element.name: OSCAL Repository
element.documentation: OSCAL Catalogs, Profiles, Components and SSPs.

element.name: Pattern & Blueprint Repository
element.documentation: Architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and solution designs.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: One graph store, two planes: Architecture Intent and Current-State Digital Twin.

element.name: Framework Pack Library
element.documentation: NIST / FedRAMP baselines; ArchiMate / C4 / UML metamodels.

element.name: Forensic Audit Ledger
element.documentation: Append-only, immutable record of agent actions, gate decisions, specification evaluations and governed state transitions, kept as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Enterprise Architect
element.documentation: Owns principles, target patterns, options and governance decisions.

element.name: Solution Architect
element.documentation: Composes blueprints into solution designs.

element.name: Security Architect / Threat Modeller
element.documentation: Runs threat models over patterns, blueprints and designs.

element.name: Developer
element.documentation: Consumes generated specifications for delivery.

element.name: Compliance Officer / Auditor
element.documentation: Authors control content and verifies traceability.

element.name: Platform Operations (BAU)
element.documentation: Watches control effectiveness and drift in run.

element.name: Source Control
element.documentation: Git repositories for specifications and delivery code.

element.name: CI/CD Pipeline
element.documentation: Builds, tests and releases; invokes the enforcement gate.

element.name: Cloud & Infrastructure Platforms
element.documentation: Runtime platforms whose live state feeds the digital twin.

element.name: IT Service Management / Backlog
element.documentation: Delivery backlog and ticketing (e.g. Jira).

element.name: Regulatory Content Sources
element.documentation: Upstream NIST OSCAL content and FedRAMP baselines.

element.name: LLM Provider
element.documentation: Language model used for drafting specs, ADRs, evaluations and threat narratives.

element.name: RFP / Vendor Submissions
element.documentation: Requests for proposal and competing vendor solution responses assessed at engagement time.

element.name: Policy & Standards Authoring
element.documentation: Author custom policy and standard content as Trestle Markdown catalogs.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog & Profile Generation
element.documentation: Convert authored Markdown and upstream baselines into OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles (Trestle round-trip).

element.name: Pattern Authoring & Control Mapping
element.documentation: Author technology-agnostic architecture patterns and map them to OSCAL Profiles.

element.name: Blueprint Authoring & Component Mapping
element.documentation: Derive implementation blueprints from patterns and map them to OSCAL Component Definitions.

element.name: Solution Design Composition
element.documentation: Compose blueprints and patterns into a solution design and emit its OSCAL System Security Plan.

element.name: Threat Modelling
element.documentation: Attach threats and mitigations to patterns, blueprints and solution designs.

element.name: Future-State & Options Modelling
element.documentation: Model one or more candidate future-state architectures, including competing vendor / RFP responses, as decision input for Architecture Governance.

element.name: Digital Twin Ingestion
element.documentation: Build the current-state digital twin plane from live infrastructure state and deployment events.

element.name: Forensic Ledger Recording
element.documentation: Append every agent action, gate decision, specification evaluation and governed state transition to the append-only Forensic Audit Ledger as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Comparative Evaluation & Decision
element.documentation: Compare candidate options, assess impact against intent and twin, record the ADR, and archive rejected options with rationale.

element.name: Controls Enforcement Gate
element.documentation: Evaluate a release candidate against the expected controls and the solution design at release time; block or pass.

element.name: Controls Effectiveness Monitoring
element.documentation: Monitor whether deployed controls remain effective in BAU and record the evidence.

element.name: Drift & Deviation Detection
element.documentation: Diff as-designed intent against the current-state twin and classify deviations as drift findings.

element.name: Modelling & Notation Rendering
element.documentation: Render ArchiMate / C4 / UML models against the bundled metamodels.

element.name: Specification Generation
element.documentation: Generate development specifications from patterns, blueprints and solution designs for spec-driven delivery.

element.name: Policy / Standard Document
element.documentation: Custom policy or standard authored as Trestle Markdown.

element.name: Regulatory Baseline Catalog
element.documentation: Upstream NIST OSCAL catalog / FedRAMP baseline.

element.name: OSCAL Catalog
element.documentation: Machine-readable control catalog.

element.name: OSCAL Profile
element.documentation: Tailored control selection / baseline.

element.name: OSCAL Component Definition
element.documentation: Control implementation claims for a reusable component.

element.name: OSCAL System Security Plan
element.documentation: Control implementation for a specific solution design.

element.name: Architecture Pattern
element.documentation: Technology-agnostic

element.name: Implementation Blueprint
element.documentation: Technology-specific realisation of one or more patterns.

element.name: Solution Design
element.documentation: Composed solution — SolutionComponents under a SolutionDesign.

element.name: Threat Model
element.documentation: Threats and mitigations attached to a pattern

element.name: Live Infrastructure State
element.documentation: Observed configuration of the running platforms.

element.name: Deployment Event
element.documentation: A release / deployment recorded by the pipeline.

element.name: Current-State Digital Twin
element.documentation: The as-built plane of the Architecture Knowledge Graph.

element.name: Candidate Architecture Option
element.documentation: A proposed future-state or vendor solution under evaluation.

element.name: Architecture Decision Record
element.documentation: The chosen option with its rationale and trade-offs.

element.name: Impact Assessment
element.documentation: Effect of a candidate option on intent and current state.

element.name: Archived Rejected Option
element.documentation: A not-chosen option retained with the reasons it lost.

element.name: Release Candidate
element.documentation: A build submitted to the enforcement gate.

element.name: Gate Decision
element.documentation: Pass / block outcome with the controls evaluated.

element.name: Control Effectiveness Evidence
element.documentation: BAU evidence that a control is (or is not) working.

element.name: Classified Drift Finding
element.documentation: A deviation of current state from intent

element.name: Remediation Backlog Item
element.documentation: A drift finding promoted to actionable delivery work.

element.name: Development Specification
element.documentation: Executable spec derived from patterns

element.name: Notation Metamodel
element.documentation: ArchiMate / C4 / UML metamodel used to constrain modelling.

element.name: Ledger Entry
element.documentation: A single immutable forensic record — actor
